Financial Highlights:

For the nine-month period ended September 30th, 2026 compared to September 30th, 2025 (all funds in Canadian dollars):

  • Total revenue decreased 11% to $527,506 from $590,573. The TLC-2000 Cool Laser Therapy system represented 87% of sales, compared to 79%.

  • Canadian revenue decreased 8% to $507,492 from $550,453; US revenue decreased 47% to $20,014 from $37,741; international revenue decreased 100% to nil from $2,379.

  • Cost of sales decreased 20% to $238,703 from $299,743.

  • Gross margin was $288,803 (55% of revenue), compared to $290,830 (49%).

  • Selling expenses increased 3% to $218,163 from $212,421.

  • Administrative expenses increased 8% to $1,556,197 from $1,444,687 (primarily reflecting increases in investor relations, administrative salaries, amortization and depreciation allocation and general administrative expenses).

  • Net research and development expenses decreased 26% to $1,570,095 from $2,116,540 (primarily due to decreased costs associated with Study II patient enrollment and treatment).

  • Net loss decreased 12% to $3,013,858 (includes $499,263 of non-cash expenses) from $3,435,145 (includes $718,197 of non-cash expenses).

  • The Drug Division accounted for $2,496,298 (83%) of the net loss.

  • Cash used in operating activities increased 24% to $2,552,478 from $2,057,733.

For the nine-month period ended September 30th, 2026 compared to December 31st, 2025 (all funds in Canadian dollars):

  • Cash increased 3838% to $7,204,200 from $182,914.

  • Working capital increased 1860% to $7,907,730 from $403,506.

  • Shareholders' equity increased 416% to $9,181,261 from $1,777,816.

  • Outstanding short-term loans decreased to nil from $255,935.

Financing Highlights

During the nine-month period ended September 30th, 2026, Theralase® successfully completed a series of brokered and non-brokered private placements, generating approximately $9.7 million in net cash proceeds.

On August 24, 2026, the Company closed a brokered private placement pursuant to the Listed Issuer Financing Exemption, issuing 14,812,500 units at $0.24 per unit for aggregate gross proceeds of $3,555,000.

These financings have significantly strengthened the Company's financial position and provided additional resources to advance its lead bladder cancer clinical program, expand its oncology pipeline and support ongoing research and development activities.

The Company has raised approximately $17.9 million over the last two years through brokered and non-brokered private placements in support of its R&D programs. The Company is working with a full-service investment bank in Canada for future financings and has identified a full-service investment bank in the United States to advise on potential financings and US listing opportunities. Additional financing remains necessary to support ongoing operations and development activities.

Operational Highlights

Phase II NMIBC Clinical Study - Cohort 1

Study II (NCT03945162) is a Phase II, open-label, single-arm, multi-center study conducted in Canada and the United States, evaluating Ruvidar® activated by the TLC-3200 Medical Laser System ("Study Procedure") in patients with BCG-Unresponsive Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer ("NMIBC") Carcinoma In-Situ ("CIS") (with or without resected papillary disease) ("Study II").

Theralase® has completed enrollment in Study II, with the CSSs enrolling and providing the primary Study Procedure to 97 patients, exceeding the 90 patients calculated in the statistical analysis plan.

Note: In the following clinical analysis, 2 patients who were considered BCG-Intolerant were removed to analyze only BCG-Unresponsive patients, leaving 95 patients in Study II.

According to the clinical study design, a patient is considered to have completed Study II, if they received the Study Procedure and have been assessed by the Principal Investigator ("PI") for up to 15 months or they have been prematurely removed from the clinical study by the PI for failure to respond or failure to comply with the clinical study design.

According to this definition, for BCG-Unresponsive patients 85 have completed Study II and 10 patients remain on study pending clinical data.

The following interim clinical data support the Study II endpoints:

Of the 95 patients enrolled and treated, 81% were ≥ 65 years of age, 82% male and 83% white. Tumor stage was distributed as follows: 82% pure CIS; 12% CIS + T1; and 6% CIS + Ta. 100% were classified as BCG-Unresponsive. The median number of BCG instillations was 12.

As of November 27th, 2026, 91 patients have been assessed for the primary endpoint, 55 for the secondary endpoint and 85 for the tertiary endpoint.

Primary Endpoint Performance (Complete Response at any Point in Time)

The primary endpoint of Study II is the achievement of CR at any point in time following the Study Procedure. Interim analysis demonstrates that 60.4% (55/91) evaluable patients achieved CR. A Total Response ("TR") was achieved by 69.2% (63/91) of evaluable patients.

Table 1: Primary Endpoint Performance

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

Note: Total Response ("TR") includes CR and Indeterminate Response ("IR"), defined as negative cystoscopy (no evidence of Urothelial Cell Carcinoma ("UCC") in the bladder) and positive / suspicious urine cytology (detection of cancer in the urine, without a negative confirmatory bladder biopsy, suggesting UCC in the renal system other than the bladder).

Secondary Endpoint Performance (Duration of CR - 12 Months)

The secondary endpoint evaluates the sustainability of CR at 12 months, after initial CR determination (450 days post-treatment). Among patients evaluable for durability of response, 40.8% (20/49) patients maintained a CR at 450 days. A TR was achieved by 44.9% (22/49) of evaluable patients. Biopsy-confirmed CR: 95%. Median follow-up: 330 days.

The current median duration of response is 9 months (95% CI: 7.2, 10.6).

The predicted median duration of response, according to Kaplan-Meier's analysis, is 12 months.

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/2786/326264_fdb6592be46b3adf_002full.jpg

Table 2: Secondary Endpoint Performance

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/2786/326264_fdb6592be46b3adf_002full.jpg

Tertiary Endpoint Performance (Safety)

The tertiary endpoint is defined as patients who have a Serious Adverse Event ("SAE") ≥ 4 directly caused by the Study Drug or Study Device, which did not resolve within 450 days.

Theralase® and the independent Data Safety Monitoring Board believe all SAEs reported to date are unrelated or unlikely related to the Study Drug or Study Device.

Note: A SAE is defined as any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose: Is serious or life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, is a congenital anomaly/birth defect or results in death.

Treatment Emergent Adverse Events ("TEAEs") were noted, but did not meet the SAE criteria. TEAEs included hematuria (73%), urinary frequency (67%) and urinary urgency (63%), which had a median resolution of 15, 36 and 43 days, respectively.

Cystectomy-free rate was 89% at 1 year and 80% at 3 years.

For Adverse Events ("AEs") reported there were: 65% Grade I, 33% Grade II, 1% Grade III and 1% Grade IV. All Grade I to Grade IV SAEs were resolved between 1 to 82 days. There were three Grade V SAEs that were considered unrelated or unlikely related to the Study Drug, Study Device or Study Procedure. Of the 25 SAEs, 92% were not TEAEs.

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/2786/326264_fdb6592be46b3adf_004full.jpg

Table 3: Tertiary Endpoint Performance

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/2786/326264_fdb6592be46b3adf_004full.jpg

Duration of CR - Extended Time Points

Patients who have completed Study II were followed for up to 3 years after initial treatment at extended time points.

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/2786/326264_fdb6592be46b3adf_005full.jpg

Table 4: Duration of CR at Extended Time Points

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/2786/326264_fdb6592be46b3adf_005full.jpg

One patient demonstrated CR for 7 years, after one Study Procedure.

On Kaplan-Meier analysis, if CR is obtained, the long term estimated probability of remaining cancer free at 1, 2 and 3 years is 52.3%, 38.2% and 27.5%, respectively.

The interim clinical results support light-activated Ruvidar® as a potential bladder-preserving treatment option for patients diagnosed with BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS, with or without papillary disease.

Regulatory Pathway, Commercialization Strategy and FDA Guidance

If approved by Health Canada and the FDA, the clinical data collected from Study II represents a transformative therapeutic option for patients diagnosed with BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS, who would otherwise face radical cystectomy (surgical removal of the bladder).

The Theralase® Study Procedure has demonstrated a robust CR and sustained durability of that response, with the majority of patients receiving only a single Study Procedure (51%).

Theralase® is currently analyzing and compiling the clinical data for a New Drug Submission to Health Canada and a New Drug Application to the United States Food and Drug Administration with marketing decisions anticipated in 2027.

In 2027, Theralase® will pursue licensing agreements of the bladder cancer technology for global marketing and distribution of light-activated Ruvidar®.

Cohort 2

Theralase®, in conjunction with Ferring Pharmaceutical, is enrolling patients into a combinational clinical study to investigate the safety and efficacy of combining light-activated Ruvidar® with Adstiladrin.

It is anticipated that the complementary mechanisms of action (Ruvidar® targets bladder cancer cells directly, Adstiladrin® targets health bladder cells to produce Interferon to stimulate the innate and adaptive immune system) will provide a strong additive effect in the treatment of patients being treated for BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS.

In the Study Procedure, patients will be treated with Ruvidar® (1 hour of drug instillation, 1 hour of light activation), then at another visit, they will be instilled with Adstiladrin® (1 hour procedure), both in outpatient procedures. Under the clinical protocol, the patient may receive up to 4 treatments of Adstiladrin® in total.

The presiding uro-oncologist will have the option to deliver an additional re-induction Study Procedure, if the patient recurs.

The patient will be followed for 15 months after initial Study Procedure and up to 3 years for post-study follow-up.

Commercialization and Strategic Partnerships

In parallel with the finalization of Study II, Theralase® is pursuing commercialization opportunities and strategic partnerships to support the global marketing and distribution of Ruvidar®. The Company is interested in engaging in discussions with pharmaceutical companies regarding:

  • Licensing arrangements for Ruvidar® in the treatment of BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS in various geographic territories
  • Collaborative clinical research initiatives focused on the application of light-activated Ruvidar® for broader NMIBC indications
  • Collaborative clinical research combining Ruvidar®, with other FDA-approved drugs to enhance treatment efficacy

Product Stability and Logistics

Ruvidar® has demonstrated a shelf life of >10 years at room temperature, which supports both the long-term stability of the molecule and the practical logistics of clinical storage and distribution. This extended shelf life is expected to be a key differentiator in clinical and commercial settings, enabling medical facilities to store and deploy Ruvidar®, as needed, without significant cold chain and degradation concerns.

Expansion of the Oncology Pipeline - Rutherrin®

On September 15th, 2026, the Company commenced Good Laboratory Practice ("GLP") toxicology analysis of intravenously administered Rutherrin®. The program is designed to determine the Maximum Tolerated Dose and Human Equivalent Dose to provide starting and therapeutic doses for future human clinical studies. Completion is expected by the end of 2026, with results anticipated in early 2027.

Subject to receipt of toxicology reports and regulatory approval, the Company plans to advance Phase 0/I/II adaptive clinical development for glioblastoma multiforme, non-small cell lung cancer and muscle-invasive bladder cancer, followed by pancreatic cancer and colorectal cancer.

Phase 0 will evaluate tumour localization; Phase I/II will evaluate safety, dosing and therapeutic efficacy following multiple doses with radiation activation. Preclinical findings support further investigation, but do not establish human safety or efficacy.

Herpes Simplex Virus Type 1 ("HSV-1")

Theralase® continues preclinical development of topical Ruvidar® for HSV-1 lesions. Laboratory research demonstrated inhibition of HSV-1 replication at lower concentrations than acyclovir and additive / synergistic effects in combination experiments. Preclinical mouse model research supports further investigation of topical Ruvidar®. Human safety and efficacy remain to be established.

Roger DuMoulin-White, President and Chief Executive Officer of Theralase®, stated: "Throughout 2026, Theralase® has focused on strengthening its financial position, advancing its lead bladder cancer clinical program and expanding its therapeutic development pipeline. With patient enrollment completed in Study II, our priority in 2027 is the analysis and compilation of the clinical data of Study II required for regulatory submissions and successful marketing approval by Health Canada and the FDA, representing an important next step toward the potential commercialization of light-activated Ruvidar®. In parallel, our collaborative clinical development agreement with Ferring Pharmaceuticals and the completion of GLP toxicology for intravenously administered Rutherrin® provide opportunities to expand the clinical application of our energy-activated small molecule technology for numerous oncological conditions. With approximately $7.2 million in cash and $7.9 million in working capital as of September 30th, 2026, Theralase® is focused on advancing these important clinical and regulatory milestones, while maintaining financial discipline and building long-term shareholder value."

About Study II

Study II utilizes the therapeutic dose of the patented drug, Ruvidar® (TLD-1433), activated by the TLC-3200 Medical Laser System. Study II has enrolled and treated 95 BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS (with or without resected Ta/T1) patients across 11 clinical study sites located in Canada and the United States.

About Adstiladrin

Adstiladrin® (nadofaragene firadenovec-vncg) is an FDA-approved intravesical non-replicating gene therapy for the treatment of adult patients with high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC CIS with or without papillary tumors (±Ta/T1). It is a non-replicating adenovirus vector-based therapy containing the gene interferon alfa-2b, administered locally as a monotherapy by catheter directly into the bladder once every three months. The vector enters the cells of the bladder wall, releasing the active gene and causing the bladder's cell walls to secrete high and transient local expression of interferon alfa-2b protein, a naturally occurring protein the body uses to fight cancer. This approach essentially turns the bladder wall cells into interferon micro factories, enhancing the body's own natural defenses against the cancer.

data.title: Mundoro Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Enhances Capital Efficiency: Appoints New CFO, Changes Auditor and Streamlines Board
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Mundoro Capital Inc. (TSXV: MUN ) (OTCQB: MUNMF) (www.mundoro.com) ("Mundoro" or the "Company") announces the filing of its condensed interim consolidated financial statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, together with a series of changes to its finance, audit and board structure designed to optimize the allocation of the Company's capital to its project portfolio.

Highlights

  • Q3 2026 results filed: corporate expenses of $1,002,990 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease of 3% compared with the same period in 2025. Cash of $2,962,438 as at September 30, 2026 and no long-term debt.

  • New Chief Financial Officer: Anil Jiwani returns to Mundoro as CFO effective December 1, 2026, succeeding James (Jim) Scott.

  • Change of auditor: Davidson & Company LLP appointed as the Company's auditor, replacing PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP. The change was initiated by the Company following a competitive proposal process.

  • Streamlined Board: the Board of Directors will be reduced from five to four directors effective December 31, 2026, three of whom are independent.

  • Strategic investment closed: The private placement by Centerra Gold Inc., previously announced on November 6, 2026, closed on November 27, 2026.

Teo Dechev, CEO, President and Director of Mundoro, stated, "In Serbia, our partner-funded exploration programs completed 4,363 metres of drilling, new AMT and gravity surveys and the re-logging of more than 20,000 metres of drilled core from various drilling campaigns over the last 10 years, advancing seven porphyry targets, five of them with drill proposals in place. We added two new senior members to our technical and operations teams, and we restructured our accounting and administration functions to optimize the use of our capital in advancing our portfolio. We also welcomed Centerra Gold as a new strategic shareholder through a private placement. We will seek new partners to advance the drill-ready targets on the eight licences in Serbia returning to 100% Mundoro ownership. Mundoro enters 2027 with funding in place, a more efficient cost structure and a clear focus on advancing opportunities across our portfolio."

Capital Efficiency and Corporate Structure

Mundoro reviews its cost structure every year with the aim of directing a greater share of its capital toward its project pipeline. In 2026, the review focused on the administration side of the business: finance, audit, governance and corporate support. The changes announced today are the outcome of that review and are designed to restructure fixed corporate costs while maintaining the quality of the Company's financial reporting and oversight. The Company also continually looks for ways to improve its workflows and efficiency across the organization.

The finance function moves to a model in which the CFO role is provided through an external firm, giving the Company access to a broader team of accounting professionals without the fixed cost of a larger in-house team. The change of auditor aligns the audit with the Company's generator business model, and a four-member Board, sized to the Company's current stage, optimizes governance costs while maintaining a majority of independent directors.

Appointment of Chief Financial Officer

Mundoro announces the appointment of Anil Jiwani, CPA, CA, as Chief Financial Officer, effective December 1, 2026. Mr. Jiwani previously served as CFO of Mundoro from 2017 to 2018 and brings a working knowledge of the Company's financial structure, partner arrangements and projects. His services will be provided through Avisar Everyday Solutions Ltd. ("Avisar"), which gives the Company access to a broader team of accounting professionals. Mr. Jiwani has more than 20 years of experience in accounting, corporate finance and public company reporting, primarily in the mining and mineral exploration sector. He is also Chief Operating Officer and a director of Avisar.

Mr. Jiwani succeeds James (Jim) Scott, who has served as CFO since July 2026, and previously from June 2022 to January 2025, and who oversaw the preparation of the Company's third quarter 2026 filings. The Board and management thank Jim for his service and contributions to the Company's financial reporting and wish him well in his future endeavours.

Change of Auditor

The Company has changed its auditor from PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP ("PwC") to Davidson & Company LLP ("Davidson"). The change was initiated by the Company following a request-for-proposal process overseen by the Audit Committee, and was not the result of a resignation by PwC. Davidson was selected for its experience with mineral exploration, generator and royalty companies, and for a cost-effective fee structure. There were no modified opinions in PwC's reports on the Company's financial statements for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, and there have been no "reportable events", as defined in National Instrument 51-102 - Continuous Disclosure Obligations ("NI 51-102"). In accordance with NI 51-102, the Notice of Change of Auditor, together with the letters from PwC and Davidson, has been reviewed and approved by the Audit Committee and the Board and filed on SEDAR+. The Company thanks PwC for its services over the last 13 years.

Change in Board Composition

As part of the organizational review and capital efficiency initiatives, the Board will be reduced from five to four directors. In connection with this reduction, Stephen Altmann will step down from the Board effective December 31, 2026. The Board and management thank Mr. Altmann for his contributions to Mundoro over the past five years and wish Stephen continued success in his future endeavours. The Board will comprise three independent directors and one non-independent director. Michael Calyniuk serves as Lead Director and will assume the role of Chair of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. Siegfried Weidner will assume the role of Chair of the Compensation Committee. Mark Platt continues to serve as Chair of the Audit Committee.

Q3 2026 Financial Highlights

For complete details of the Company's financial results, please refer to the condensed interim consolidated financial statements and MD&A for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The Company's filings are available on SEDAR+ and on Mundoro's website at www.mundoro.com under the heading Investors. All amounts are expressed in Canadian dollars unless otherwise indicated.

Fees Earned: The Company's fee income, which includes operator fees, option payments, interest, and miscellaneous income, totaled $287,039 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to $246,566 for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $40,473. The increase was driven by higher operator fee income recognized during Q3 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

Exploration Expenditures: Exploration expenditures, represent both sole funded exploration by partners and expenditures for generative activities for the Company, together those were $2,767,738 in Q3 2026 compared to $1,710,067 in Q3 2025, representing an increase of $1,057,671. Recoveries from option partners in Q3 2026 were $2,701,888 compared to $1,354,720 in Q3 2025.

Generative Activities: Generative activities create long-term royalty opportunities and may generate future property payments, milestone payments, and other fees through the optioning of mineral projects to third parties. Included in total exploration expenditures are net exploration costs attributable to the Company's generative operations in the three jurisdictions where it is active and which are funded by the Company. These expenditures resulted in $65,850 in Q3 2026 compared to $355,347 in Q3 2025.

Corporate Expenses: Corporate expenses in Q3 2026 were $379,897 compared to $369,862 in Q3 2025, representing an increase of $10,035.

Cash and Working Capital: As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents totaling $2,962,438 (December 31, 2025 - $5,217,157) and a working capital (current assets less current liabilities) of $1,064,255 (December 31, 2025 - $1,684,464). The decrease in cash of $2,254,719 during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily driven by cash used in operating activities, partly offset by investing inflows. This cash balance includes $1,530,801 of net advances from partners, which is required to be used on exploration activities.

Net Income (Loss): For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a net loss of $269,840 ($0.00 per share) compared to a net loss of $412,352 ($0.00 per share) for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, representing a decrease in net loss of $142,511.

data.title: Southwest Heritage Bank Announces Acquisition Agreement with Peak Credit Union
data.description:
SCOTTSDALE, AZ / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Southwest Heritage Bank, together with the bank's parent company, Bancorp 34, Inc. , today announced a definitive agreement for Peak Credit Union ("Peak") to acquire Southwest Heritage Bank. Under the agreement, Peak would acquire substantially all of Southwest Heritage Bank's assets and assume substantially all of its liabilities in an all-cash transaction.

The transaction was unanimously approved by the boards of directors of Peak Credit Union, Southwest Heritage Bank, and Bancorp 34, Inc. The acquisition is subject to customary regulatory and stockholder approvals and is expected to be completed in the second half of 2027. Following completion of the transaction, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. will dissolve and the remaining assets will be distributed to the stockholders of Bancorp 34, Inc. Subject to the terms of the agreement, stockholders are expected to receive an estimated $20.67 to $22.18 per share for an aggregate transaction value of $ 159 million to $171 million.

Peak intends to retain members of Southwest Heritage Bank's executive leadership team in senior roles within the combined organization, drawing on their expertise and experience to guide a successful integration and contribute to the credit union's long-term growth and strategic direction. In particular, Southwest Heritage Bank President Paul Tees will be responsible for leading commercial banking across the combined organization, bringing the bank's commercial lending expertise and local-market-led, relationship focused approach to Peak's broader network.

Peak also intends to retain all Southwest Heritage Bank employees immediately upon closing, subject to ordinary business and individual circumstances, to ensure continuity of service and the successful integration of the organizations' systems and processes.

Until the transaction closes, both organizations will continue to operate independently, and there is nothing customers or members need to do.

D.A. Davidson & Co. served as financial advisor and Otteson Shapiro LLP served as legal counsel to Bancorp 34, Inc. and Southwest Heritage Bank. McQueen Financial Advisors served as financial advisor and Luse Gorman, PC served as legal counsel to Peak Credit Union.

Bancorp 34, Inc. is the holding company for Southwest Heritage Bank. The bank's headquarters are located at 8777 East Hartford Drive, Suite 100, Scottsdale, Arizona 85255. In addition, the bank operates seven full-service community bank branches, two in Maricopa County, Arizona, in the cities of Scottsdale and Gilbert; three in Pima County, Arizona, in the cities of Tucson and Green Valley; one branch in Otero County, New Mexico in the city of Alamogordo; and one branch in Dona Ana County New Mexico, in the city of Las Cruces.

About Peak Credit Union: Peak Credit Union is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative serving more than 250,000 members through 35 branches across Washington and Oregon and digital banking services. Each Warrant is exercisable to purchase one additional Share (a "Warrant Share") for a period of 24 months from the closing date at an exercise price of $0.10 per Warrant Share.

The Company may complete multiple closings of the Offering, as subscriptions are received.  Each closing is subject to a number of conditions, including receipt of all necessary corporate and regulatory approvals.

The Company intends to use the net proceeds from the Offering for working capital, and general and administrative expenses. Securities issued under the Offering will be subject to a hold period which will expire four months and one day from the date of closing of the Offering.

In addition to the Offering, the Company may also settle up to $200,000 in outstanding debt through Units with the same terms as issued in the Offering (the "Debt Settlement").

data.title: Ranchero Gold Announces Change of Auditor, Property Option Amendment, and Grant of Restricted Share Units
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Ranchero Gold Corp. ("Ranchero" or the "Company") announces that Smythe LLP, Chartered Professional Accountants (the "Former Auditor"), has resigned as auditor of the Company effective November 24, 2026, and that the Board of Directors has appointed Truster Zweig Raithatha LLP ("TZR"), as successor auditor effective the same date. TZR will hold office until the close of the Company's next annual meeting of shareholders, at which shareholders will be asked to approve its appointment.

The change was considered by the Audit Committee and approved by the Board. There were no modified opinions in the Former Auditor's reports for the financial years ended December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2025, and there have been no "reportable events" as defined in National Instrument 51-102 - Continuous Disclosure Obligations ("NI 51-102"). The Notice of Change of Auditor, together with the response letters of the Former Auditor and TZR, will be filed on SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.ca) in accordance with NI 51-102.

The Company thanks Smythe LLP for its services and looks forward to working with TZR.

Sandspit Option Amendment

Ranchero has also amended its option agreement dated February 28, 2025 with Homegold Resources Ltd. and Johan Thom Shearer for the Sandspit Gold Project on Moresby Island, Haida Gwaii, British Columbia. The final $100,000 option payment, previously due by February 28, 2027, has been restructured as $6,000 due by that date and $100,000 due by February 28, 2028, extending the option period by twelve months. Total cash consideration is now $118,000, of which $12,000 has been paid. The amendment also updates the claim schedule: the property comprises five mineral claims totaling 166 hectares, compared with the 398 hectares previously reported, following a reduction in the area of tenure 1120426. All other terms are unchanged.

Grant of Restricted Share Units

The Company also announces that it has granted 4,150,000 restricted share units ("RSUs") to certain directors and officers of the Company under its Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan. The RSUs vest twelve (12) months from the date of grant and, once vested, will be settled in common shares of the Company, subject to the terms and conditions of the Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan.

Martyn Buttenshaw, a director of the Company and a "qualified person" under National Instrument 43-101, has reviewed and approved the technical information in this news release.

About Ranchero Gold

Ranchero is an exploration and development company currently focused on early-stage gold exploration. Ranchero has the option to earn a 100% interest in the Sandspit gold project, consisting of five mineral claims totalling 166 hectares, situated immediately south of Sandspit, Haida Gwaii, off the coast of British Columbia, Canada. The Company continues to look for additional projects to add to its portfolio.

data.title: Peak Credit Union Announces Agreement to Acquire Southwest Heritage Bank
data.description:
The proposed acquisition would deepen business banking expertise and expand Peak's reach into Arizona and New Mexico

EUGENE, Ore. and LACEY, Wash. and SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Peak Credit Union announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire all assets and assume all liabilities of Southwest Heritage Bank, a subsidiary of Bancorp 34, Inc. (), in an all-cash transaction.

The proposed acquisition would bring together Peak's broad consumer financial services and member-owned cooperative model with Southwest Heritage's commercial lending expertise, treasury management services, and established business relationships across Arizona and New Mexico. The combination is intended to expand the financial resources available to individuals and business owners while preserving the local expertise and personal relationships valued by Southwest Heritage customers.

"Our focus is on finding meaningful ways to serve more people," said Dr. David L. Tuyo II, president and CEO of Peak Credit Union. "We know many of our members already spend part of the year in Arizona, making it a natural place for us to grow. Southwest Heritage has built trusted relationships with local businesses, backed by people who understand their communities. Bringing that expertise together with Peak's broader capabilities gives us an opportunity to help more people and businesses move toward their financial goals."

Over time, Peak members could benefit from deeper commercial lending and treasury management capabilities, while Southwest Heritage customers could gain access to additional consumer financial services. Specific products, eligibility, and timing will be determined as integration planning progresses.

The employees and relationships of Southwest Heritage Bank are central to the value of the planned transition. Peak intends to retain Southwest Heritage employees at closing, subject to ordinary business and individual circumstances, to support service continuity and integration. Peak also intends to retain members of Southwest Heritage's executive leadership team in senior roles. Final roles and reporting relationships remain subject to approval and integration planning.

There are no immediate changes to branch operations, accounts, or banking services as a result of today's announcement. Until the transaction closes, the two organizations are expected to continue to operate independently, and members and customers do not need to take any action. It is expected that Peak will communicate any future changes directly and in advance.

The boards of directors of Peak Credit Union, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. approved the agreement unanimously. The transaction remains subject to customary regulatory and shareholder approvals and is expected to close in the second half of 2027.

Following closing, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. is expected to dissolve and distribute the remaining assets of Bancorp 34, Inc. to its shareholders in accordance with the transaction terms.

D.A. Davidson & Co. served as financial advisor and Otteson Shapiro LLP served as legal counsel to Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. McQueen Financial Advisors served as financial advisor and Luse Gorman, PC served as legal counsel to Peak Credit Union.

About Peak Credit Union: Peak Credit Union is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative serving more than 250,000 members through 35 branches across Washington and Oregon and digital banking services. Formed from the combination of TwinStar Credit Union and Northwest Community Credit Union, Peak brings a longstanding commitment to financial education, accessible financial services and community well-being. Through the PeakCU Foundation, Peak supports local initiatives including classroom grants, scholarships and financial education. Federally insured by NCUA. Equal Housing Opportunity. Learn more at peakcu.org.

About Southwest Heritage Bank: Southwest Heritage Bank, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, is a community-focused bank serving individuals and businesses in Arizona and New Mexico. The bank offers commercial lending, treasury management and personal financial services, with an emphasis on local relationships and responsive service. Southwest Heritage Bank is a subsidiary of Bancorp 34, Inc. (). Member FDIC. Learn more at swhbank.com.

data.title: S&P revises Hungary outlook to stable as fiscal risks ease
data.description:
Credit ratings agency S&P on Friday revised Hungary's outlook to stable from negative, saying strong institutional and fiscal frameworks would ensure a steady decline in budgetary deficits over the next two years.

The outlook revision follows six months of reforms by Prime Minister Peter Magyar that improved ties with European Union institutions, unlocking €16.4 billion in previously suspended EU funding and easing concerns over the country's financing outlook.

"We forecast that Hungary’s economic activity will rebound in 2027 and remain steady through 2029," the agency said.

Magyar Nemzeti Bank, the Hungarian central bank, has grown more cautious amid renewed pressure on the forint. Having signaled room for a rate cut as early as next month, it adopted a more guarded tone after dovish remarks pushed the currency to a seven-month low last week.

However, S&P added that forint appreciation has mitigated commodity price volatility. The agency also affirmed the sovereign's rating at "BBB-/A-3".

The decision aligns S&P with peer Moody's, which last week lifted Hungary's outlook to stable while affirming its sovereign rating at "Baa2".
